why_ai: A licensed officer must swear the witness and certify the record personally, often in the room, but speech recognition and digital capture press on the transcription half of the work.
why_clarity: A certified verbatim transcript is an exact, checkable deliverable produced under codified formats, though errors surface only when errata or disputes test a page.
why_digital: Spoken testimony in a room or on a call is turned into text on a screen and delivered digitally, but buyers book licensed reporters venue by venue.

why_ai: Coverage still means a licensed reporter at the deposition or on the call, and agencies sell availability more than any one person.
why_clarity: Covered or not and on time or not are clear outcomes, recurring thousands of times a year with known booking rules.
why_digital: Bookings arrive digitally and much testimony is now remote, but coverage depends on licensed people in each venue.

why_ai: Transcripts can be produced from court audio away from the courtroom, but certification under court rules and statutory pricing keep a licensed officer accountable.
why_clarity: Statutory page formats, delivery tiers and appellate deadlines make the deliverable exact and the procedure codified.
why_digital: Court audio or steno notes in and transcripts filed electronically, bought through court contracts and orders rather than an open market.

why_ai: An examination under oath needs an officer present to swear and record the claimant, and the certificate of non-appearance is a sworn act.
why_clarity: Appearance, transcript and signature are clear outcomes against the carrier's claim clock.
why_digital: Claimants appear in person or by video and paperwork moves by mail, though transcripts are delivered digitally.

why_ai: Hearings need a reporter or recording in the room, but certification rules are looser than in court and forums can switch to recording.
why_clarity: Each forum's format and turnaround define a checkable deliverable that recurs across many hearings.
why_digital: Capture happens at the hearing, production and delivery are digital, and contracts are won forum by forum.

why_ai: Serving unrepresented litigants means a certified record of an in-person hearing, and demand grows as courts stop staffing these calendars.
why_clarity: Whether a reviewable record exists is clear, but which hearings will matter is a judgement and the outcome arrives months later on appeal.
why_digital: The hearing and the litigant are local and in person, with requests on paper and little online buying.

why_ai: Remote live captioning is screen work exposed to automatic captions, protected mainly by technical content and a user who relies on a particular captioner.
why_clarity: Accuracy against what was said is measurable and sessions recur, though reference transcripts are costly to make.
why_digital: Audio in, live text out, delivered remotely by captioners anywhere.

why_ai: Editing a raw capture into clean text is where speech recognition and AI editing tools are aimed, softened only by scopists' ties to particular reporters and the certification step that keeps digital transcripts tied to a licensed officer.
why_clarity: A transcript is checkable against the audio and the work recurs page after page.
why_digital: Files in, files out, worked remotely by freelance editors.

why_ai: Scoping is screen work that AI editing tools now reach, protected only by the scopist's knowledge of one reporter's writing.
why_clarity: Correct translation of each stroke is checkable against audio, on near-identical jobs.
why_digital: CAT files and audio in and out, worked remotely.

why_ai: Machine drafts do most of the transcription, leaving certification and acceptance as the protected step.
why_clarity: A transcript is checked against multi-channel audio, job after job, with clear formats.
why_digital: Recordings and annotations in, transcripts out, worked by remote pools; certification rules tie it to states.

why_ai: Rule-driven clocks, document handling and distribution are routine back-office work that automation absorbs.
why_clarity: Every step has a defined rule, a deadline and an instant check of whether it happened.
why_digital: Documents and notices move entirely online.

why_ai: Search over transcripts is exposed to AI, but challenge research rests on a contributed corpus and bar relationships that keep buyers loyal.
why_clarity: Testimony histories are well defined, but how useful a report proved shows only when the motion is decided.
why_digital: Transcripts in, research reports out, sold online to members.

why_ai: Bespoke policy studies for courts and legislatures rest on institutional trust and contested judgement.
why_clarity: Each study is one-off, methods vary, and whether the recommendation was right is known years later.
why_digital: Data and interviews in and reports out, though studies involve site visits and are bought by named public bodies.

why_ai: Spend analysis and vendor negotiation are screen work, with judgement on panel design and neutrality risk.
why_clarity: Rates, spend and turnaround are measurable and recur across thousands of claims.
why_digital: Invoices and vendor data in, guidelines and reports out, all digital.

why_ai: Their product is the AI substitution itself, competing with general legal AI tools.
why_clarity: A summary is fairly well defined and recurs per transcript, though quality is judged by the lawyer reading it.
why_digital: Transcripts in, summaries out, sold as software online.

why_ai: Software for a licensed trade, protected by switching costs in reporters' dictionaries but exposed as capture moves to audio.
why_clarity: Translation and realtime features have checkable behaviour on recurring tasks.
why_digital: Software built and sold digitally to a professional user base.

why_ai: Storing, copying and summarising transcripts is routine digital work that AI absorbs.
why_clarity: Copies, deliveries and summaries are defined outputs repeated per transcript.
why_digital: Entirely online storage and delivery.

why_ai: Credit decisions on case outcomes involve judgement, but the product is a payment term.
why_clarity: Repayment is measurable but known only when cases resolve, often years later.
why_digital: Applications and payments are handled online.

why_ai: Certification exams, advocacy and member relationships rest on trust and in-person events.
why_clarity: Certifications are defined, but advocacy outcomes are slow and contested.
why_digital: A mix of in-person testing, conventions and lobbying with online services.

why_ai: Advocacy and certification for newer capture methods rest on legislative relationships that AI does not replace.
why_clarity: Certifications are defined; whether advocacy succeeds is known only after legislative cycles.
why_digital: Mostly online certification and communication, with in-person lobbying.

why_ai: Statutory authority to license and discipline cannot be delegated to software.
why_clarity: Exams, licences and complaint rules are codified and recur.
why_digital: Exams and hearings are partly in person and the board serves one state.

why_ai: Rule-setting by the judiciary is an accountable public function.
why_clarity: Rates and policies are defined, but whether they keep courts staffed shows only over years.
why_digital: Policy work is digital, but the buyer and audience are the federal courts alone.

why_ai: Courtroom installation and support are partly physical, and the software competes with general recording and ASR products.
why_clarity: Recording systems have checkable specifications and recurring installations.
why_digital: Hardware installed in courtrooms, software and support delivered remotely, sold through court procurement.

why_ai: Sell-side advice rests on relationships with owners and buyers and judgement on each deal.
why_clarity: Each deal is bespoke and its success is known only after closing and integration.
why_digital: Mostly remote work, but trust is built with owners face to face.
